content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in Rust: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `src/main.rs`. Build and run it with `cargo` and `clippy`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. total 24 drwxr-xr-x 7 vshynkarenko staff 224 11 Okt. 13:31 . drwxr-xr-x 3 vshynkarenko staff 96 11 Okt. 13:31 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1830 11 Okt. 13:31 BRIEF.md -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 151 13 Sep. 17:42 Cargo.lock -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 91 13 Sep. 17:41 Cargo.toml drwxr-xr-x 3 vshynkarenko staff 96 13 Sep. 17:41 src drwxr-xr-x 5 vshynkarenko staff 160 13 Sep. 17:42 target

content.text:
The four additions are in `src/main.rs`, and the program builds and passes clippy with no warnings. I checked it with one sample command file, not a full test suite. - **`prio

`**: sets the priority and writes `prio

`. Tasks default to priority 5. - **Error cases**: an unknown id writes `no such task `, and a `p` that isn't a single digit 0–9 writes `bad priority

` and changes nothing. If both are wrong, the unknown id is reported. - **`list`**: open tasks are ordered by priority, then id, with the same line format as before. - **`list all`**: every task, same order, as ` ` with `-` for open and `x` for finished. - **Unknown commands**: a line whose first word isn't a command writes `? <word>`. - **`add`, `done`, `list`**: unchanged. Beyond the brief: - A line holding only whitespace is treated as blank and stays silent, as it did before. - A non-numeric id given to `prio` writes `no such task <text>` rather than panicking. The sample run covered priorities, a finished task, an unknown command and both list forms, and each line matched the brief.
